description: Create or revise a Verification — a check that something meets its intent. `method` says HOW you looked: test, analysis, inspection and demonstration are the four canonical ones, plus measurement, observation (watching it run in the field, unchanged), review and simulation. Answers the `build_without_verification` and `unverified_capability` gaps. Its `verifies` list says what it checks, on a new check or an existing one. ⚠️ KEEP `name` SHORT — it is what a list renders. Put the account of what the check IS in `description`, and what a RUN FOUND in `findings` on set_verification_status. Measured on reflow2's own graph before those were reachable: median Verification name 76 words, longest 654, because `description` was declared and this constructor had no parameter for it, so everyone wrote reports into the name. CONTENT FIELDS ARE REQUIRED TO CREATE AND OPTIONAL TO REVISE: call it again with the same id and only what you are changing — omitted fields keep their stored value, so correcting one never means re-sending a 2 KB field you did not touch.

VerifyTargetReq.description: One target of a Verification, for `add_verification`'s `verifies` list.

target_id.description:
The node this check verifies — a Requirement (`req:…`), Capability
(`cap:…`), Interface or any node a VERIFIES edge may reach. Its type is
resolved from the id; `target_type` names it when the id is ambiguous.

target_type.description:
Node type being verified. Optional: resolved from the id when omitted;
an id held by more than one type is REFUSED, never guessed.

computed.description:
MADE BY COMPUTATION: a calculator, a script or a solver produced the
result. Then, as a premise of an Inference, a `passing` check holds
only through its KEPT RECORD — an Artifact with a checksum that
DOCUMENTS the check, that it PRODUCES, or that `location` names — and
with none it reads `asserted` (unknown). A `location` naming a
`.calc.json` record makes it computed without this. Omitted: nothing is
written.

description.description:
What the check IS, at length — the account a reader needs that does not
fit in `name`. PUT IT HERE RATHER THAN IN `name`: on reflow2's own graph
the median Verification name was 76 words and the longest 654, because
this field was declared and had no parameter to reach it. What a RUN
FOUND is a different thing and goes to `findings` on
set_verification_status.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

findings.description: What that run FOUND. Refused without `status`: a finding belongs to a run.

fixes.description:
THE VARIABLES IT BINDS TO ONE VALUE, each `name=value` (`n=40`, `L=all
the primes`) or a bare name. A step that generalizes over a variable
does not hold while anything it rests on fixes it. Omitted: nothing is
written.

hypothesis_block.description:
A HYPOTHESIS TEST FROM flo2-calc: the `hypothesis_test` object of the
tested value in its kept record (record schema 10), passed exactly as
the record holds it. Needs `test`, `alpha.value`, `p_value.value`, `n`,
`decision` and `reject_h0`; a block missing one is refused by its path
and nothing is written. It marks the check computed, writes each of its
`assumptions` as a Constraint the check DEPENDS_ON (taken as given, so
an objection can attack it), draws CONSTRAINS from the α Constraint its
`alpha.source.design_node` names (with the record's α as the
`contribution` when that Constraint has a `limit`; one already drawn is
kept), and on the first call locks its criteria. As a premise it then
reads "supported at α (p, test, n)", never proof, or "not rejected at
α".

id.description: The verification's id — `ver:<slug>` by convention, so the prefix names the type wherever the id appears. Calling again with an EXISTING id REVISES that node: what you pass overwrites, what you omit survives.

last_run_at.description: When that run happened. Refused without `status`, for the same reason.

location.description:
PATH TO THE TEST OR INSPECTION ARTIFACT — the file a reader opens to see
what this check actually does.

Offered since 2026-09-20 (flo2 F19): the property was declared and
documented, and no typed tool accepted it, so the path had to go in
`description` or through the generic escape hatch.

method.description:
HOW the check was made. `test` (default) / `analysis` / `inspection` /
`demonstration` — the four canonical methods — plus `measurement`,
`observation` (watching it run in the field, unchanged), `review` and
`simulation`.

status.description:
The outcome of a run you have ALREADY TAKEN — `planned` / `passing` /
`failing` / `skipped` / `blocked` — for the common case "I just ran it
and here is what it found". Omit it and the check lands `planned`.

variables.description:
THE VARIABLES IT MENTIONS, by name (`n`, `L`): free in what it checks. Shown on a step that
generalizes over one. Omitted: nothing is written.

verifies.description:
What this check VERIFIES, as a list of objects shaped
`{"target_id": "cap:x", "target_type": "Capability"}` with `target_type`
optional, drawn in the same call — one VERIFIES edge per entry.
`target_type` may be omitted (resolved from the id). Recording
one check used to take four to six calls
(dec:idea-should-a-constructor-accept-the-owners-word-in-one-call).
